    // =========================================================================
// Models/Formulaires.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The fields in the "person" forms and their constraints. Three
// forms share the same identity fields (title, first name, last name):
//
//    ChampsPersonn               e title, first name, last name
//     ├─ FormulairePerson       ne + login / password FACULTATIFS, version
//                                   │ (ADMIN adds or modifies a doctor/client)
//     ├─ FormulaireInscripti    on + login / password / confirmation OBLIGATOIRES
//                                   │ (a patient creates an account)
//     └─ FormulaireMonComp      te + username, optional new password,
//                                    ACTUEL password required, version
//                                    (a patient modifies their account)
//
// LIAISON DE MODÈLE (model binding): when a controller action receives
// a parameter from one of these classes, ASP.NET Core MVC creates the object and
// populates each property with the form field of the same name (without
// case sensitivity: the “name” field populates the Name property).
//
// VALIDATION: Immediately afterward, MVC checks the attributes [Required],
// [MaxLength]... (standard namespace System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations,
// the equivalent of `class-validator`) and stores the errors in ModelState.
// The controller then simply needs to test ModelState.IsValid.
//
// The error messages are translation strings (see i18n/*.json).
//
// NETTOYAGE DE LA SAISIE (the equivalent of @Transform in class-transformer):
//    - MVC already converts an empty field to null;
//    - the setters below remove unnecessary spaces and set the
//      login in lowercase. A password, however, is not "cleaned" (
//      spaces may be part of it).
// All properties are “nullable” (string?): a field may still
// be missing in the data sent by the browser; [Required] requires it.
// =========================================================================

using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;

namespace RdvMedecins.Models;

public static class ReglesSaisie
{
    public static readonly string[] Titres = ["Mr", "Mme", "Melle"];

     // login: lowercase letters, numbers, period, hyphen, underscore—30 characters maximum
    public const string FormatLogin = "^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$";

     // minimum password length for a patient: CHOISI
    public const int MotDePasseMin = 6;

     / / " dupont " -> "dupont"  ; " " -> null
    public static string? Nettoyer(string? valeur) => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(valeur) ? null : valeur.Trim();
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A "custom" validation attribute: the value must be included in a list.
// Simply inherit from ValidationAttribute and write IsValid.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public class ParmiAttribute(params string[] valeurs) : ValidationAttribute
{
     // null is accepted here: it is the role of [Required] to require it
    public override bool IsValid(object? value) => value is null || valeurs.Contains(value as string);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ common base
public class ChampsPersonne
{
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE")]
    [Parmi("Mr", "Mme", "Melle", ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE")]
    public string? Titre { get; set; }

     // maximum lengths = those of the columns SQL (VARCHAR(20))
    private string? prenom;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED")]
    [MaxLength(20, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Prenom
    {
        get => prenom;
        set => prenom = ReglesSaisie.Nettoyer(value);
    }

    private string? nom;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED")]
    [MaxLength(20, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Nom
    {
        get => nom;
        set => nom = ReglesSaisie.Nettoyer(value);
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ ADMIN
public class FormulairePersonne : ChampsPersonne
{
    private string? login;

     // optional (see DonneesPersonne, Business Line/IMetier.cs)
    [RegularExpression(ReglesSaisie.FormatLogin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")]
    public string? Login
    {
        get => login;
        set => login = ReglesSaisie.Nettoyer(value)?.ToLowerInvariant();
    }

     // optional; 72 characters maximum (if longer, bcrypt ignores the rest)
    [MaxLength(72, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Password { get; set; }

     // hidden field in the edit form (optimistic lock).
     // int? : a missing or empty field returns null; text that is not a
     // number results in a binding error (see Program.cs, ModelBindingMessageProvider)
    public int? Version { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ patient registration
public class FormulaireInscription : ChampsPersonne
{
    private string? login;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED")]
    [RegularExpression(ReglesSaisie.FormatLogin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")]
    public string? Login
    {
        get => login;
        set => login = ReglesSaisie.Nettoyer(value)?.ToLowerInvariant();
    }

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_REQUIRED")]
    [MinLength(ReglesSaisie.MotDePasseMin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT")]
    [MaxLength(72, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Password { get; set; }

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED")]
    public string? Confirmation { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ "Manage My Account"
public class FormulaireMonCompte : ChampsPersonne
{
    private string? login;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED")]
    [RegularExpression(ReglesSaisie.FormatLogin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")]
    public string? Login
    {
        get => login;
        set => login = ReglesSaisie.Nettoyer(value)?.ToLowerInvariant();
    }

     // optional: blank = password unchanged
    [MinLength(ReglesSaisie.MotDePasseMin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT")]
    [MaxLength(72, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Password { get; set; }

    public string? Confirmation { get; set; }

     // The password ACTUEL, required for any account changes
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED")]
    public string? MotDePasseActuel { get; set; }

    public int? Version { get; set; }
}

    Let's discuss this code:

    • line 43: possible titles;
    • line 46: the format of a username, described by a regular expression: 1 to 30 characters consisting of lowercase letters, digits, a period, a hyphen, and an underscore;
    • line 49: the minimum length of a password chosen by a patient. This is a constant ([const]), so it can be used as an argument for an attribute, such as [[MinLength(ReglesSaisie.MotDePasseMin)]] below;
    • line 52: cleaning up an entry: leading and trailing spaces are removed, and a field consisting solely of spaces becomes [null], meaning it is invalid;
    • lines 59–62: a validation attribute we wrote: the value must appear in a list. All we need to do is derive it from [ValidationAttribute] and redefine [IsValid]. [null] is accepted: it is the role of [[Required]] to reject a missing field. We use it under the name [[Parmi]]: by convention, the suffix [Attribute] can be omitted;
    • Line 66: the identity fields, common to all three forms. All properties are of type [string?]: a field may always be missing in the data sent by the browser, and it is [[Required]] that requires it. Error messages are translation keys (see Example 22);
    • Lines 68–70: the title, which is required and selected from the list. The values are repeated in [[Parmi(...)]]: an attribute’s argument must be known at compile time, which is not the case for the array [ReglesSaisie.Titres] (a [static readonly] field, created at runtime);
    • lines 73–80 and lines 83–90: the first name and last name, which are required and may be up to 20 characters long (the width of the SQL columns). These properties have a body: their value is stored in a private field, and [set] cleans it up as it passes through. Since the model binding affects the properties before validation, it is the cleaned-up value that is validated. This is equivalent to the [@Transform] in version [NestJS]; [ASP.NET Core MVC] already automatically converts an empty field to [null];
    • line 95: the ADMIN form, for adding or editing a doctor or a client. The class inherits the identity fields and their validation attributes;
    • lines 97–104: the login, which is optional here but must be in the correct format if present (line 100); it is sanitized and converted to lowercase. [?.] calls [ToLowerInvariant] only if the value is not [null];
    • lines 108–109: the password, also optional, with a maximum of 72 characters: the [bcrypt] algorithm, which encrypts it, ignores any characters following it. A password is not sanitized: spaces are included as part of it;
    • line 114: the record’s version, in a hidden field of the update form (optimistic lock; see Example 28). A missing or empty field results in [null]; text that is not a number produces a binding error, whose message is configured in [Program.cs] (see Example 19);
    • Line 118: A patient creates an account: username, password (6 to 72 characters, line 131), and confirmation (lines 135–136) are required. Verifying that the password matches its confirmation involves two fields: this is checked by the validator ([Controllers/InscriptionController.cs]);
    • Line 140: A patient modifying their account. The new password is optional (line 153): if left blank, the password remains unchanged; its confirmation (line 157) is therefore not required here. The current password, however, is required for any changes (lines 160–161), and the record version is stored in a hidden field (line 163).

    // =========================================================================
// Models/ModelesVues.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// "View models": what each controller passes to
// its view (return View("...", model)), in a C# class TYPÉE. In a
// Razor view, @model AgendaModele declares the model type: the compiler
// then checks every @Model.Xxx in the view—a typo results in a
// compilation error, not an empty section on the page.
//
// A rule already followed with Handlebars: no logic in views. The
// controllers prepare formatted data DÉJÀ ("Ms. Marie
// PELISSIER", "8:00 - 8:20", Selectionne = true...) and already filtered according to
// the user’s role; the views simply place them in the HTML.
// =========================================================================

namespace RdvMedecins.Models;

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// what TOUTES the pages have in common, as read by the template
// (Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public abstract class ModeleVue
{
     // translation key for the page title (<title>)
    public string TitrePage { get; set; } = "APP.TITLE";

     // LE page error message, displayed at the bottom of the page
     // (see Views/Shared/_Erreurs.cshtml); null = no error
    public string? Erreur { get; set; }

    public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? ErreurParams { get; set; }
}

// an option from a drop-down list (doctor, patient)
public record OptionVue(int Id, string Libelle, bool Selectionne);

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ login
public class LoginModele : ModeleVue
{
    public string Login { get; set; } = "";
    public required Auth.Captcha Captcha { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ calendar
public class LigneAgendaVue
{
    public int IdCreneau { get; init; }
    public string Horaire { get; init; } = ""; // "8:00 - 8:20"
    public bool Libre { get; init; }
    public string? Patient { get; init; } // display name for a booked time slot; null = “Reserved”
    public bool Moi { get; init; } // the logged-in patient’s appointment
    public bool Reservable { get; init; } // Display the "Book" button?
    public string UrlReserver { get; init; } = "";
    public int? IdRv { get; init; } // filled in only if the "Cancel" button is displayed
}

public record AgendaVue(string Medecin, string Jour, List<LigneAgendaVue> Lignes);

public class ReservationVue
{
    public int IdCreneau { get; init; }
    public string Horaire { get; init; } = "";
     // ADMIN / DOCTOR: the list of patients to choose from
    public List<OptionVue> Clients { get; init; } = [];
     // USER: the patient is the patient themselves
    public string? Patient { get; init; }
}

public class AgendaModele : ModeleVue
{
    public List<OptionVue> Medecins { get; set; } = [];
    public int? IdMedecin { get; set; }
    public string Jour { get; set; } = ""; // "yyyy-MM-dd"
    public AgendaVue? Agenda { get; set; }
    public ReservationVue? Reservation { get; set; }
    public string UrlRetour { get; set; } = "/agenda"; // the displayed calendar, without the booking window
     // Patient who already has an upcoming appointment: the explanatory message
     // why there is no “Book” button
    public string? Info { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ "Person" forms

// the values displayed in the form fields (never the password)
public class ValeursPersonne
{
    public string Titre { get; set; } = "Mr";
    public string Prenom { get; set; } = "";
    public string Nom { get; set; } = "";
    public string Login { get; set; } = "";
    public int? Version { get; set; }
}

// what the common partial _ChampsPersonne.cshtml uses (title, first name, last name)
public abstract class FormulaireVue : ModeleVue
{
    public ValeursPersonne Valeurs { get; set; } = new();

     // field -> key of the message displayed SOUS this field (input error)
    public Dictionary<string, string> Erreurs { get; set; } = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

     // fields to be highlighted in red (Bootstrap "is-invalid" class): those that have
     // a message, plus any others (duplicate first name + last name, login already taken...)
    public HashSet<string> ChampsInvalides { get; set; } = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

    public string? ErreurDe(string champ) => Erreurs.GetValueOrDefault(champ);

    public string ClasseInvalide(string champ) => ChampsInvalides.Contains(champ) ? "is-invalid" : "";

    public IEnumerable<(string Valeur, bool Selectionne)> Titres =>
        ReglesSaisie.Titres.Select(t => (t, t == Valeurs.Titre));
}

public class FormulairePersonneModele : FormulaireVue
{
    public bool Creation { get; set; } // true: add; false: update
    public string Action { get; set; } = ""; // URL from POST
    public string UrlListe { get; set; } = "";
}

public class InscriptionModele : FormulaireVue
{
    public int MotDePasseMin => ReglesSaisie.MotDePasseMin;
}

public class MonCompteModele : FormulaireVue
{
    public int MotDePasseMin => ReglesSaisie.MotDePasseMin;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ lists of doctors / clients

// translation keys specific to each person type
public record ClesPersonnes(
    string Titre, // "Doctors"
    string Ajouter, // "Add a doctor"
    string Modifier, // "Edit a doctor"
    string Vide, // "No doctors."
    string ConfirmerSuppression, // "Delete this doctor and their account?"
    string Ajoute, // "The doctor {name} has been added (login: {login})."
    string Modifie,
    string Supprime);

public record PersonneVue(string Titre, string Prenom, string Nom, string Login, string UrlModifier, string UrlSupprimer);

public class ListePersonnesModele : ModeleVue
{
    public required ClesPersonnes Cles { get; set; }
    public string UrlAjouter { get; set; } = "";
    public List<PersonneVue> Personnes { get; set; } = [];
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ patient area
public record RendezVousVue(int Id, string Jour, string Horaire, string Medecin, string UrlAgenda);

public class EspaceModele : ModeleVue
{
    public string Patient { get; set; } = "";
    public List<RendezVousVue> RendezVous { get; set; } = [];
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ error page
public class ErreurModele : ModeleVue
{
    public int Code { get; set; }
    public string Message { get; set; } = "ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR";
}

    The view templates follow the rule already applied with [Handlebars]: no logic in the views. The controllers prepare data that is already formatted (“Ms. Marie PELISSIER,” “8:00 – 8:20”) and already filtered according to the user’s role; the views simply place this data into the HTML. Each view declares the type of its template ([@model AgendaModele], see Example 13): the compiler checks each [@Model.Xxx], and a typo results in a compilation error.

    Let’s comment on this code:

    • lines 22–31: what all pages have in common, as read by the [_Layout.cshtml] template: the translation key for the page title (line 25), and the page’s error message, displayed at the bottom, along with its parameters. The class is abstract: each page has its own template, which derives from it;
    • line 35: an option from a drop-down list (a doctor, a patient), already marked as selected or unselected (see Example 18);
    • lines 38–41: the login page: the username already entered and the CAPTCHA to be displayed. The keyword [required] requires the person creating the object to assign a value to the property; failing to do so results in a compilation error;
    • lines 45–54: a calendar entry, i.e., a time slot. The controller has already determined everything: whether the patient’s name is displayed (a patient cannot see the names of others), whether the “Reserve” button is displayed, and whether the “Cancel” button is displayed ([IdRv] is set). The properties [init] can only be assigned a value when the object is created;
    • Line 57: A doctor's schedule for a single day: the doctor's name, the day spelled out in full, and the lines;
    • Lines 59–66: The appointment window: the list of patients for ADMIN and the doctors, or just the name of the logged-in patient;
    • lines 69–79: the calendar page: the list of doctors, the selected doctor and day, the calendar ([null] as long as no doctor is selected), the booking window (if present), the calendar URL without this window (line 76), and the message explaining to a patient why they cannot book an appointment;
    • lines 85–91: the values displayed in the fields of a “person” form, never the password: a password is not sent back to the browser;
    • line 95: the parent class of the templates for the three “person” forms, the one required by [Validation.Preparer]: the field values, the messages below the fields (line 100), and the fields to be highlighted in red (line 104). A [HashSet] is a set: each element appears only once, and the membership test is fast;
    • Lines 106–108: two methods for views: a field’s message (or [null]), and the class [Bootstrap] [is-invalid], which frames a field in red. Views are named, for example, [@Model.ClasseInvalide("login")];
    • lines 110–111: the options in the title list, with the selected option marked (see Example 18). Each option is a tuple [(Valeur, Selectionne)];
    • lines 114–118: the ADMIN form, used for adding and modifying entries (see Example 28): the mode, the form submission URL, and the list URL for the back button;
    • lines 121–128: the registration and account management forms; they pass the minimum password length to the view, which is used as the [{min}] parameter for the field’s error message and, for registration, for the help text;
    • lines 134–142: the doctor and client management pages are the same views; only their text differs. This [record] contains the translation keys specific to each type of person;
    • lines 144–150: a row in the list of doctors or clients, with the addresses of its Edit and Delete buttons, and the template for the list page;
    • lines 154–159: the patient’s area: their name and upcoming appointments, each with a link to the daily calendar;
    • lines 163–166: the error page: the code HTTP and the message key, which by default is that of a server error.

    11.16. The Web Layer: Controllers

    Controllers are the visible part of the web layer: each one receives requests from a group of pages, reads their parameters, queries the business layer (always through the [ApplicationModel] service), then selects a view and passes it a typed model, or redirects the request. All POST forms follow the Post/Redirect/Get pattern (see Example 20); all messages are translation keys, translated by the view. The connection controller, [AuthController], has been commented out for authentication.

    // =========================================================================
// Controllers/LangueController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// GET /language/fr, GET /language/en: the two buttons FR / EN on the
// navigation bar. Unsecured route: it should be possible to change the language before
// logging in.
//
// The selection is stored in LE a cookie in the localization middleware
// of ASP.NET Core (CookieRequestCultureProvider, see Program.cs): with each
// subsequent request, this middleware re-reads it and sets the request’s language
// (CultureInfo.CurrentCulture / CurrentUICulture). Then we return to the
// page we came from.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Localization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

public class LangueController : Controller
{
    [HttpGet("langue/{langue}")]
    public IActionResult Changer(string langue)
    {
        if (!Traducteur.Langues.Contains(langue))
        {
            return NotFound(); // -> 404 error page (see Program.cs)
        }
        Response.Cookies.Append(
            CookieRequestCultureProvider.DefaultCookieName,
             // cookie value: "c=en|uic=en" (format language, text language)
            CookieRequestCultureProvider.MakeCookieValue(new RequestCulture(langue)),
            new CookieOptions { MaxAge = TimeSpan.FromDays(365), SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax, HttpOnly = true, Path = "/" });
        return Redirect(PageDOrigine());
    }

     // the previous page, based on the "Referer" header HTTP sent by the
     // browser. We only keep the path (/agenda?...): redirect to
     // a complete address provided by the request would allow us to send
     // the user to a different site (a vulnerability known as an “open redirect”).
    private string PageDOrigine()
    {
        var referer = Request.Headers.Referer.ToString();
        if (!Uri.TryCreate(referer, UriKind.Absolute, out var url))
        {
            return "/";
        }
        return url.AbsolutePath.StartsWith("/langue/", StringComparison.Ordinal) ? "/" : url.PathAndQuery;
    }
}

    This is, except for one line, the controller from Example 22: same route [/langue/{langue}], same localization middleware cookie, same return to the original page via the header [Referer]. Two clarifications:

    • line 34: the option [Path = "/"] makes the cookie valid for all addresses on the site, regardless of the page from which the language was changed;
    • line 49: if the original page is itself a [/langue/...] page, the user is redirected to the site’s root rather than back to that page, which would cause the browser to go in a loop.

    // =========================================================================
// Controllers/AgendaController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The calendar page: selecting a doctor and a day, that
// doctor’s schedule for that day, booking and canceling appointments.
//
//    GE T /agenda?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-2             3 the page
//    GE T /agenda?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-23&reserve=7    the same page, with
//                                                           the booking window
//                                                           for time slot 7 is open
//    POST /calendar/book                                   creates an appointment
//    POST /calendar/canc                                  el cancels an appointment
//
// The entire page is described by its URL: you can reload it, add it
// to favorites, or use the browser’s “Back” button—without a single line
// of JavaScript.
//
// What everyone sees and can do:
//
//    | rol         e | displayed re           served slot           | Reserve | Cancel |
//   |---------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
//    | ADMIN, DOCTOR | patient name                         | for     a patient | yes |
//                  |                                    |            | selected from list | |
//    | USER (patient)| “Reserved,” or SON name if it i s | for himself, if he| no (*) |
//                  | | his own            appointment          | does not already have an appointment| |
//                  |                                                         | | upcoming | |
//
//    (*) The patient cancels their appointment from their "My Account" page.
//
// CONFIDENTIALITÉ: for a patient, the names of the AUTRES patients are not
// simply hidden by the view—it is never included in the template
// passed to the view. The HTML sent to the browser therefore does not contain it,
// nor is it hidden (otherwise, simply “View Source” would reveal it).
//
// No reservations in the past: the “Reserve” button only appears
// for today and the following days (and the business layer would reject it
// in any case).
//
// [Authorize] on the class: all actions require a logged-in user
// (equivalent to @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)). [Authorize(Roles =
// "...")] on an action also requires one of the listed roles (RolesGuard +
// @Roles). Without a valid token: redirect to /login; insufficient role: 403 page.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Metier;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

[Authorize]
[Route("agenda")]
public class AgendaController(ApplicationModel application) : Controller
{
     // what the controller knows about the user to determine what to display
    private record Droits(
        bool Gestionnaire, // ADMIN or DOCTOR
        Client? Patient, // the logged-in client (role USER), otherwise null
        bool PatientPeutReserver); // USER with no upcoming appointments
    • Lines 7–12: the page’s routes. Note that the booking window is not opened by [JavaScript]: it is a parameter of URL ([reserver=7]) that instructs the server to render the page with the window open. The “Book” button is therefore simply a link. The entire page is described by its URL: you can reload it, bookmark it, or use the browser’s “Back” button;
    • lines 18–28: what each role sees and can do. This table is the page’s “specification”: the rest of the controller implements it;
    • lines 30–33: the privacy rule, which we’ll come back to: the names of other patients are not hidden by the view; they are never sent to the browser;
    • lines 55–57: [[Authorize]] on the class: all actions require a logged-in user, regardless of their role (see Example 25). [[Route("agenda")]] is the prefix for all routes in the controller (see Example 02). The controller receives the [ApplicationModel] service via injection (see Example 06) through its main constructor: the parameters written in parentheses after the class name are accessible in all of its methods;
    • lines 60–63: what the controller knows about the logged-in user, calculated once per request (see [DroitsAsync], below). A private [record], declared inside the class: it is used only by that class. A handler is a ADMIN or a DOCTOR; [Patient] is populated only for a client (role USER).

        // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /calendar
     // The parameters of URL are read in raw format (Request.Query), to distinguish
     // a ABSENT parameter from a VIDE parameter (?idMedecin=).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Afficher()
    {
        string? erreur = null;
        var utilisateur = User.Utilisateur()!;
        var droits = await DroitsAsync(utilisateur);

         // the day: the one from URL if it is valid, otherwise today
        var jour = Dates.Aujourdhui();
        if (Request.Query.TryGetValue("jour", out var jourBrut))
        {
            if (DatesWeb.EstUneDateValide(jourBrut, out var jourDemande))
            {
                jour = jourDemande;
            }
            else
            {
                erreur = "ERRORS.INVALID_DATE";
            }
        }
        var jourReservable = jour >= Dates.Aujourdhui();

         // the doctor: the one from URL; otherwise, for a logged-in doctor, the doctor themselves
        var idMedecin = Saisie.EntierPositif(Request.Query["idMedecin"]);
        if (!Request.Query.ContainsKey("idMedecin") && utilisateur.Role == Role.DOCTOR)
        {
            idMedecin = application.GetMedecinByUserId(utilisateur.UserId)?.Id;
        }

        var medecins = (await application.GetAllMedecinsAsync())
            .Select(m => Option(m, m.Id == idMedecin))
            .ToList();

         // the calendar, if a doctor is selected (and the date is valid)
        AgendaVue? agenda = null;
        if (idMedecin is int id && erreur is null)
        {
            var agendaMedecin = await application.GetAgendaMedecinJourAsync(id, jour);
            if (agendaMedecin is null)
            {
                erreur = "ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND";
            }
            else
            {
                var lignes = agendaMedecin.CreneauxMedecinJour.Select(cmj =>
                {
                    var (creneau, rv) = (cmj.Creneau, cmj.Rv);
                    var libre = rv is null;
                     // the logged-in patient’s appointment?
                    var moi = rv is not null && droits.Patient is not null && rv.IdClient == droits.Patient.Id;
                    return new LigneAgendaVue
                    {
                        IdCreneau = creneau.Id,
                        Horaire = DatesWeb.Horaire(creneau),
                        Libre = libre,
                         // LE privacy setting: a patient only receives the name
                         // for the SON appointment; for others, null (the view displays “Reserved”)
                        Patient = rv is not null && (droits.Gestionnaire || moi) ? Libelles.Libelle(rv.Client) : null,
                        Moi = moi,
                        Reservable = libre && jourReservable && (droits.Gestionnaire || droits.PatientPeutReserver),
                        UrlReserver = UrlAgenda(id, jour, creneau.Id),
                        IdRv = rv is not null && droits.Gestionnaire ? rv.Id : null,
                    };
                }).ToList();
                agenda = new AgendaVue(Libelles.Libelle(agendaMedecin.Medecin), DatesWeb.Iso(jour), lignes);
            }
        }
    • Lines 6–7: the route [GET /agenda] (controller prefix, followed by an empty string). The action has no parameters: it automatically reads URL as [Request.Query] (see Example 05). The model binding would convert a [int? idMedecin] parameter to [null] whether it is missing or empty; however, these two cases must be distinguished (see below);
    • Lines 10–11: the logged-in user and their permissions. [Utilisateur()] is an extension method (see Example 06) defined in [Auth/UtilisateurConnecte.cs]: it reads the token’s claims and converts them into a typed object. [!] informs the compiler that the result is not [null]: this is certain, since [[Authorize]] has filtered out unauthenticated requests;
    • lines 14–26: the requested day, if valid; today otherwise. [TryGetValue] returns [false] if the parameter [jour] is missing: in that case, it returns today, without a message. If present but invalid ([jour=2026-02-30]), it generates an error message. Reservations can only be made starting today ([jourReservable]);
    • lines 29–32: the requested doctor. [Saisie.EntierPositif] (record [Web]) returns a strictly positive integer, or [null] if the value is missing, empty, or invalid. If the [idMedecin] parameter is missing from URL, a logged-in doctor sees their own schedule: this is their home page. If it is empty ([idMedecin=], the “Choose a Doctor” option in the list), no schedule is displayed;
    • lines 35–37: the options in the doctors’ drop-down list, read from the cache of [ApplicationModel]; the option for the requested doctor is selected (see the [Option] function at the end of the file and Example 18);
    • lines 40–46: The schedule is calculated only if a doctor is selected and the date is valid. [idMedecin is int id] checks that the value (of type [int?]) is not [null], and stores its value in a new variable [id], of type [int]. An unknown doctor ID triggers a message, not an error page;
    • lines 50–56: The schedule calculated by the business layer (a [AgendaMedecinJour] object from the [Domain] record) is converted into array elements, one per time slot. [var (creneau, rv) = ...] breaks down a value pair into two variables. [moi] determines whether the appointment belongs to the logged-in patient;
    • Lines 58–59: The view receives only data that has already been formatted ([8:00 - 8:20]); it no longer has anything to calculate;
    • line 63: the application’s privacy control. The patient’s name is included in the model only for an administrator or for the patient whose appointment it is. For everyone else, the model contains [null], and the view displays “Reserved.” The name is not simply hidden by the view: it is never sent to the browser, and “View Page Source” would not reveal it;
    • lines 65–67: what the view must display, as determined by the controller: the “Reserve” button (available time slot, date not past, and user authorized to reserve), its link (the page’s URL, with [reserver]), and the “Cancel” button ([IdRv] is populated only for an administrator). The view does not make any decisions: it follows these instructions;
    • line 70: the complete schedule: the doctor, the day, the rows.

        ReservationVue? reservation = null;
        var idCreneau = Saisie.EntierPositif(Request.Query["reserver"]);
        var ligne = agenda?.Lignes.FirstOrDefault(l => l.IdCreneau == idCreneau && l.Reservable);

                    ? (await application.GetAllClientsAsync()).Select(c => Option(c, false)).ToList()
                    : [],
                Patient = droits.Patient is not null ? Libelles.Libelle(droits.Patient) : null,
            };
        }

        return View("Agenda", new AgendaModele
        {
            TitrePage = "AGENDA.PAGE_TITLE",
            Medecins = medecins,
            IdMedecin = idMedecin,
            Jour = DatesWeb.Iso(jour),
            Agenda = agenda,
            Reservation = reservation,
            UrlRetour = idMedecin is int idm ? UrlAgenda(idm, jour) : "/agenda",
            Info = droits.Patient is not null && !droits.PatientPeutReserver ? "AGENDA.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO" : null,
            Erreur = erreur,
        });
    }
    • lines 3–5: the time slot for which URL is requesting a reservation ([reserver=7]). It must appear in the displayed schedule and be bookable by this user: a manually created URL (a past time slot, a booked time slot, or a slot for another doctor) does not open the window. [agenda?.Lignes] is equivalent to [null] if [agenda] is [null] (operator [?.]);
    • lines 6–15: the window template. An administrator selects a patient from a list (all clients, read from the cache); a patient makes a reservation for themselves: the window simply displays their name. [[]] is an empty list;
    • lines 19–29: the page template. Its classes ([AgendaModele], [AgendaVue], [LigneAgendaVue], [ReservationVue], [OptionVue]) are defined in [Models/ModelesVues.cs]; [TitrePage] and [Erreur] are derived from their common parent class [ModeleVue]. [TitrePage] is, like all texts, a translation key;
    • line 27: the address of the displayed calendar, without the booking window—this is the address of the button that closes the window;
    • line 28: an informational message for patients who already have an upcoming appointment: it explains why they do not see a “Book” button.

        // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /calendar/boo  k fields: idMedecin, day, idCreneau, idClient
    //
     // For a patient (USER), the field idClient is IGNORÉ: they book
     // always books for himself. Trusting a field sent by the
     // browser would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation in someone else’s name.
    //
     // "Post/Redirect/Get" pattern: regardless of the result, we do not
     // generate a page here—we post a flash message and redirect
     // to the calendar (see Web/Flash.cs).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("reserver")]
    [Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN,DOCTOR,USER")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Reserver(
        [FromForm] string? idMedecin,
        [FromForm] string? jour,
        [FromForm] string? idCreneau,
        [FromForm] string? idClient)
    {
        if (!LireAgendaDemande(idMedecin, jour, out var idMed, out var jourDemande)
            || Saisie.EntierPositif(idCreneau) is not int idCre)
        {
            return BadRequest(); // -> “Invalid request” page (see Program.cs)
        }

        Client? client;
        if (User.IsInRole(nameof(Role.USER)))
        {
            client = await Patient.PatientConnecteAsync(application, User);
        }
        else
        {
            if (Saisie.EntierPositif(idClient) is not int idCli)
            {
                 // No patient selected: the booking window reopens
                Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT");
                return Redirect(UrlAgenda(idMed, jourDemande, idCre));
            }
            client = await application.GetClientByIdAsync(idCli);
        }

        var creneau = await application.GetCreneauByIdAsync(idCre);
        if (client is null)
        {
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND");
        }
        else if (creneau is null || creneau.IdMedecin != idMed)
        {
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.SLOT_NOT_FOUND");
        }
        else
        {
            try
            {
                 // the rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment per
                 // patient, available time slot) are verified by the business layer
                await application.AjouterRvAsync(jourDemande, creneau, client);
                Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, "AGENDA.BOOKED");
            }
             // "when": an exception filter. Same rule, but a message to the second
             // person when the patient makes the appointment themselves (“You have
             // already...” rather than “This patient...””)
            catch (MetierException e) when (e.Cle == "ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT" && User.IsInRole(nameof(Role.USER)))
            {
                Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "AGENDA.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO");
            }
             // any other MetierException becomes a flash message; the other
             // exceptions (true errors) are not caught: 500 page
            catch (MetierException e)
            {
                Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, e.Cle, new Dictionary<string, string>(e.Parametres));
            }
        }
        return Redirect(UrlAgenda(idMed, jourDemande));
    }
    • Lines 12–13: [[Authorize(Roles = ...)]] on the action is added to the class’s [[Authorize]]: all three roles can make reservations (see Example 26). Here, this attribute imposes no further restrictions; it documents the rule and would protect it if a fourth role were to appear;
    • lines 15–18: the fields in the reservation window form (see Example 11). They are received as strings and then carefully converted;
    • lines 20–23: the doctor and the day are hidden fields in the form; they allow the user to return to the displayed calendar. If they are invalid, the request did not originate from our page: it was manually crafted. [BadRequest()] returns a 400 response with no content, which the [UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute] middleware transforms into an error page (see Example 24). [is not int idCre] is the opposite of [is int]: true if the value is [null]; otherwise, [idCre] receives the value;
    • Lines 27–29: For a patient, the [idClient] field is ignored—the system always makes the reservation for the patient itself. Relying on this field, which is sent by the browser, would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation in someone else’s name. [Patient.PatientConnecteAsync] (record [Web]) identifies the client using the token; [nameof(Role.USER)] is the string ["USER"], verified by the compiler;
    • Lines 33–39: A manager who has not selected a patient is redirected to the booking window (URL with [reserver]), accompanied by a pop-up error message. [Flash.Deposer] (record [Web]) stores the message in [TempData] (see Example 20);
    • lines 42–49: the patient must exist, and the time slot must exist and belong to the doctor in the calendar: you cannot book a time slot belonging to one doctor for another;
    • lines 57–58: The business rules (not in the past, slot available, only one upcoming appointment per patient) are verified by the business logic layer, which raises a [MetierException] in case of rejection;
    • Lines 63–65: [when] adds a condition to [catch]: it is an exception filter [C#]. This block only catches the [MetierException] if the condition is true: for a patient, the message “this patient already has an appointment” is replaced by a second-person message. Otherwise, the exception proceeds to the next [catch];
    • lines 69–71: any other [MetierException] becomes a flash message, along with its key and parameters ([e.Parametres] is a read-only dictionary: a copy is made of it, of the type expected by [Flash.Deposer]). The other exceptions are not caught: these are true errors, which result in a 500 error page;
    • Line 74: the PRG schema: regardless of the result, a flash message is displayed and the user is redirected to the calendar, which will display the message. In version [NestJS], a utility function handled this business error conversion; here, the two [catch] blocks are sufficient.

        // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /calendar/ca  ncel fields: idRv, idMedecin, day
     // (a patient cancels SON an appointment from "My Account," not from here)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("annuler")]
    [Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN,DOCTOR")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Annuler([FromForm] string? idRv, [FromForm] string? idMedecin, [FromForm] string? jour)
    {
        if (!LireAgendaDemande(idMedecin, jour, out var idMed, out var jourDemande)
            || Saisie.EntierPositif(idRv) is not int id)
        {
            return BadRequest();
        }
        var rv = await application.GetRvByIdAsync(id);
        if (rv is null)
        {
             // already canceled (by someone else, or by double-clicking)
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND");
        }
        else
        {
            await application.SupprimerRvAsync(rv);
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, "AGENDA.CANCELLED");
        }
        return Redirect(UrlAgenda(idMed, jourDemande));
    }
    • lines 5–7: Cancellation is restricted to administrators; a patient cancels their appointment from “My Account” (see [EspacePatientController]). A patient who sends this request would receive a 403 page;
    • Lines 9–12: The same checks as for the reservation;
    • lines 14–18: An appointment that has already been canceled (by double-clicking or by another administrator) triggers an error message, not an error page;
    • lines 22–25: deletion, followed by schema PRG.

        // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // Who is logged in, and what permissions do they have on this page?
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private async Task<Droits> DroitsAsync(UtilisateurConnecte utilisateur)
    {
        if (utilisateur.Role != Role.USER)
        {
            return new Droits(Gestionnaire: true, Patient: null, PatientPeutReserver: false);
        }
        var patient = await Patient.PatientConnecteAsync(application, User);
        var rvAVenir = await application.GetRvAVenirClientAsync(patient.Id);
        return new Droits(Gestionnaire: false, patient, PatientPeutReserver: rvAVenir.Count == 0);
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- utility functions

     // the hidden fields idMedecin / day, common to both forms POST
    private static bool LireAgendaDemande(string? idMedecinBrut, string? jourBrut, out int idMedecin, out DateOnly jour)
    {
        idMedecin = Saisie.EntierPositif(idMedecinBrut) ?? 0;
        return DatesWeb.EstUneDateValide(jourBrut, out jour) && idMedecin > 0;
    }

    private static string UrlAgenda(int idMedecin, DateOnly jour, int? reserver = null)
    {
        var url = $"/agenda?idMedecin={idMedecin}&jour={DatesWeb.Iso(jour)}";
        return reserver is null ? url : $"{url}&reserver={reserver}";
    }

    private static OptionVue Option(Personne p, bool selectionne) => new(p.Id, Libelles.Libelle(p), selectionne);
}
    • lines 4–12: An administrator has full permissions; a patient can make a reservation if they have no upcoming appointments. The named arguments ([Gestionnaire: true]) make the call to the [record] constructor readable;
    • lines 18–21: reading the two hidden fields common to the POST forms. The [out] parameters are additional results from the method: it returns a Boolean (are the fields valid?) and, via its [out] parameters, the converted values. This is the process of [int.TryParse];
    • lines 24–27: the URL for a doctor’s schedule on a given day, possibly with the booking window open. All controller redirects generate this via this function: the URL for the page are written in a single location;
    • line 30: a drop-down list option (ID, label, selection), for both a doctor and a client: the parameter is of type [Personne], the parent class of both entities.

    // =========================================================================
// Controllers/PersonnesControllerBase.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Physician management and client management (reserved for ADMIN) are
// IDENTIQUES: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than
// writing the same actions twice, we write them once in this
// class ABSTRAITE and GÉNÉRIQUE, from which MedecinsController inherits
// ([Route("medecins")]) and ClientsController ([Route("clients")]). Each
// subclass simply needs to specify its “configuration”: which methods
// to call, and which labels to display.
//
// The routes defined in ICI ([HttpGet("ajouter")]...) are inherited, and
// supplement the subclass’s route. Thus, for each one, we obtain:
//
//    GE T /doctor                  s list
//    GE T /doctors/add            empty form
//    POST /doctors/add            create
//    GE T /doctors/{id}/edit      pre-filled form
//    POST /doctors/{id}/edit      edit
//    POST /doctors/{id}/delete     deletion
//
// (and the same URL under /clients). The views are also shared:
// Views/People/Liste.cshtml and Views/People/Formulaire.cshtml.
//
// An abstract class is never treated as a controller by MVC: only
// its concrete subclasses are.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Metier;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

// what each subclass must provide
public record ConfigPersonnes<T>(
    string Url, // "/doctors" or "/clients"
    ClesPersonnes Cles,
    Func<Task<List<T>>> Lister,
    Func<int, Task<T?>> Trouver,
    Func<DonneesPersonne, Task<T>> Ajouter,
    Func<int, DonneesPersonne, Task<T>> Modifier,
    Func<int, Task> Supprimer) where T : Personne;

public abstract class PersonnesControllerBase<T>(ApplicationModel application) : Controller where T : Personne
{
    protected ApplicationModel Application { get; } = application;

    protected abstract ConfigPersonnes<T> Config { get; }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /doctors (or /clients)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Liste()
    {
        var personnes = await Config.Lister();
        return View("~/Views/Personnes/Liste.cshtml", new ListePersonnesModele
        {
            TitrePage = Config.Cles.Titre,
            Cles = Config.Cles,
            UrlAjouter = $"{Config.Url}/ajouter",
            Personnes = personnes
                .Select(p => new PersonneVue(p.Titre, p.Prenom, p.Nom, p.User?.Login ?? "",
                    $"{Config.Url}/{p.Id}/modifier", $"{Config.Url}/{p.Id}/supprimer"))
                .ToList(),
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /doctors/add
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("ajouter")]
    public IActionResult FormulaireAjout() => AfficherFormulaire(null, new ValeursPersonne());

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /doctors/add
     // [formulaire] has been filled out ET validated by MVC: ModelState indicates whether the
     // entry is correct.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("ajouter")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Ajouter(FormulairePersonne formulaire)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return AfficherFormulaire(null, ValeursSaisies(formulaire), Validation.ErreursDe(ModelState));
        }
        try
        {
            var personne = await Config.Ajouter(Donnees(formulaire));
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, Config.Cles.Ajoute, Parametres(personne));
            return Redirect(Config.Url);
        }
        catch (MetierException e)
        {
            return AfficherErreurMetier(null, ValeursSaisies(formulaire), e);
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /doctors/{id}/edit
     // {id:int} : a "route constraint"—/doctors/abc/edit does not
     // corresponds to any route (404 page)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("{id:int}/modifier")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> FormulaireModification(int id)
    {
        var personne = await Config.Trouver(id);
        if (personne is null)
        {
            return NotFound();
        }
        return AfficherFormulaire(id, new ValeursPersonne
        {
            Titre = personne.Titre,
            Prenom = personne.Prenom,
            Nom = personne.Nom,
            Login = personne.User?.Login ?? "",
            Version = personne.Version,
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /doctors/{id}/edit
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("{id:int}/modifier")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Modifier(int id, FormulairePersonne formulaire)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return AfficherFormulaire(id, ValeursSaisies(formulaire), Validation.ErreursDe(ModelState));
        }
        try
        {
            var personne = await Config.Modifier(id, Donnees(formulaire));
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, Config.Cles.Modifie, Parametres(personne));
            return Redirect(Config.Url);
        }
        catch (MetierException e)
        {
            return AfficherErreurMetier(id, ValeursSaisies(formulaire), e);
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /doctors/{id}/delete
     // (The browser prompts for confirmation—"Are you sure?"—before
     // the form is submitted; see wwwroot/js/app.js)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("{id:int}/supprimer")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Supprimer(int id)
    {
        var personne = await Config.Trouver(id);
        try
        {
            await Config.Supprimer(id);
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, Config.Cles.Supprime, Parametres(personne));
        }
        catch (MetierException e)
        {
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, e.Cle, new Dictionary<string, string>(e.Parametres));
        }
        return Redirect(Config.Url);
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- private methods

     // id null: create form; otherwise: update form
    private ViewResult AfficherFormulaire(
        int? id,
        ValeursPersonne valeurs,
        Dictionary<string, string>? erreurs = null,
        string? erreur = null,
        IEnumerable<string>? autresChamps = null)
    {
        var creation = id is null;
        return View("~/Views/Personnes/Formulaire.cshtml", Validation.Preparer(
            new FormulairePersonneModele
            {
                TitrePage = creation ? Config.Cles.Ajouter : Config.Cles.Modifier,
                Creation = creation,
                Action = creation ? $"{Config.Url}/ajouter" : $"{Config.Url}/{id}/modifier",
                UrlListe = Config.Url,
                Valeurs = valeurs,
            },
            erreurs, erreur, autresChamps));
    }

     // A business rule rejected the write operation: the form is redisplayed,
     // with the user’s input and the message from the business layer
    private IActionResult AfficherErreurMetier(int? id, ValeursPersonne valeurs, MetierException e)
    {
        if (e.Cle is "ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND" or "ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND")
        {
             // deleted in the meantime by another ADMIN: return to the list
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, e.Cle);
            return Redirect(Config.Url);
        }
         // the message moves to the bottom of the page; the relevant fields, if any, are
         // highlighted in red so the user can immediately see what to correct
        return AfficherFormulaire(id, valeurs, null, e.Cle, Validation.ChampsErreursMetier.GetValueOrDefault(e.Cle));
    }

     // what the user entered (excluding the password: it is never sent back to the browser)
    private static ValeursPersonne ValeursSaisies(FormulairePersonne f) => new()
    {
        Titre = f.Titre ?? "",
        Prenom = f.Prenom ?? "",
        Nom = f.Nom ?? "",
        Login = f.Login ?? "",
        Version = f.Version,
    };

     // the submitted form -> the data expected by the business layer
    private static DonneesPersonne Donnees(FormulairePersonne f) => new()
    {
        Titre = f.Titre!,
        Nom = f.Nom!,
        Prenom = f.Prenom!,
        Login = f.Login,
        Password = f.Password,
        Version = f.Version,
    };

     // {name} and {login} for the "added / modified / deleted" messages
    private static Dictionary<string, string> Parametres(Personne? personne) => personne is null
        ? new() { ["nom"] = "", ["login"] = "" }
        : new() { ["nom"] = $"{personne.Prenom} {personne.Nom}", ["login"] = personne.User?.Login ?? "" };
}

    The management of doctors and clients is identical. Rather than writing two similar controllers, we write their actions once, in an abstract and generic parent class. Let’s comment on this code:

    • lines 15–20: the routes for doctors; the same ones exist in [/clients];
    • lines 22–23: the views are also shared (file [Views/Personnes]);
    • lines 25–26: MVC accepts only concrete classes as controllers: only [MedecinsController] and [ClientsController] receive requests;
    • lines 38–45: the configuration provided by each subclass: the base URL, the texts (translation keys, grouped in [record] and [ClesPersonnes] from [Models/ModelesVues.cs]), and the functions to be called for listing, searching, adding, modifying, and deleting. [Func<int, Task<T?>>] is the type of a function that takes a [int] and returns a [Task<T?>]: this is how methods are stored in properties, to be called later. [where T : Personne] is a constraint on the generic type: [T] will be either [Medecin] or [Client], two classes derived from [Personne]; the code can therefore use [p.Prenom] or [p.User], which are common to all people;
    • Line 47: the parent class, which is generic (see the [PageVue<TModel>] class in Example 22) and abstract. It receives [ApplicationModel] via its main constructor and passes it to its subclasses via the protected property [Application] ([protected]: visible only to subclasses);
    • line 51: an abstract property: each subclass must define it;
    • lines 56–69: the list. The route attributes set on a parent class’s methods are inherited: combined with the subclass’s [[Route("medecins")]], they yield [GET /medecins]. For each person, the model contains the URL for their Edit and Delete buttons. [p.User?.Login ?? ""]: the login for the associated account, or an empty string if the person does not have an account;
    • line 60: the view is specified by its full path. If only its name were used, MVC would search for it in the controller’s folder ([Views/Medecins] or [Views/Clients], see Example 13), whereas it is shared by both;
    • lines 75–76: the empty form;
    • lines 83–98: the addition, in three steps, as in Example 28. The parameter [formulaire] was populated and validated by MVC prior to the call (see Example 19): an invalid entry redisplays the form, showing the entered values and a message below each incorrect field; a valid entry is passed to the business layer, then the browser is redirected to the list, with a flash message (PRG); a rejection by the business layer (a homonym, a login already in use) re-displays the form;
    • Lines 107–121: the pre-filled modification form. The route constraint [:int] (see Example 02) only accepts an integer identifier: [/medecins/abc/modifier] does not correspond to any route, resulting in a 404 page ([ParseIntPipe] derived from [NestJS] resulted in a 400 error). A nonexistent person also results in a 404. The version number, a hidden field in the form, will be used for the optimistic lock (see example 28);
    • lines 128–143: the update, following the same pattern as the insertion;
    • lines 152–165: deletion. The person is retrieved beforehand to display their name in the confirmation message. A rejection from the business layer (e.g., a doctor who has appointments) results in a flash error message on the list page;
    • lines 171–188: the form for creation ([id] is equivalent to [null]), as for modification: only the title and mailing address change. [Validation.Preparer] (file [Web]) populates the template with field-specific error messages, the footer message, and the fields to be highlighted in red;
    • lines 193–203: a person who has since been deleted (by another administrator) is listed again; other business errors re-display the form, with the footer message and the affected fields highlighted in red ([Validation.ChampsErreursMetier] associates each error code with its corresponding fields: [prenom] and [nom] for a homonym). [is "A" or "B"] compares a value to several constants;
    • lines 207–213: the values to be redisplayed—never the password;
    • lines 217–224: the data transmitted to the business layer. The [!] fields pose no risk: validation has verified the presence of these fields;
    • lines 228–230: the [{nom}] and [{login}] parameters in the success messages: the person’s first and last name, and their login.

    // =========================================================================
// Controllers/MedecinsController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Physician management (ADMIN role only). All actions are
// inherited from PersonnesControllerBase: all that remains here is to specify QUOI
// "Call" and QUELS "Display" labels.
//
// [Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN")] set on CLASSE applies to all its
// actions, including inherited ones.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

[Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN")]
[Route("medecins")]
public class MedecinsController(ApplicationModel application) : PersonnesControllerBase<Medecin>(application)
{
    protected override ConfigPersonnes<Medecin> Config => new(
        Url: "/medecins",
        Cles: new ClesPersonnes(
            Titre: "MEDECINS.TITLE",
            Ajouter: "MEDECINS.ADD",
            Modifier: "MEDECINS.EDIT",
            Vide: "MEDECINS.EMPTY",
            ConfirmerSuppression: "MEDECINS.DELETE_CONFIRM",
            Ajoute: "MEDECINS.ADDED",
            Modifie: "MEDECINS.UPDATED",
            Supprime: "MEDECINS.DELETED"),
        Lister: Application.GetAllMedecinsAsync,
        Trouver: Application.GetMedecinByIdAsync,
        Ajouter: Application.AjouterMedecinAsync,
        Modifier: Application.ModifierMedecinAsync,
        Supprimer: Application.SupprimerMedecinAsync);
}
    • Lines 20–22: Reserved for ADMIN. The attribute set on the class applies to all its actions, including inherited ones. The controller inherits from [PersonnesControllerBase<Medecin>]: the parent class’s type, [T], becomes [Medecin]. Its main constructor passes [application] to the parent class’s constructor. (In [TypeScript], an explicit constructor had to be written so that [NestJS] would know what to inject; there is no need for that here);
    • lines 24–34: the configuration. [override] redefines the parent class’s abstract property; [=>] turns it into a computed property, which creates the object each time it is read. The named arguments ([Url:], [Cles:]...) make the list readable;
    • lines 35–39: the functions to be called, which are methods of [ApplicationModel]. [Application.GetAllMedecinsAsync], written without parentheses, does not call the method: it refers to it, and the compiler converts it to a value of the expected type [Func].

    // =========================================================================
// Controllers/InscriptionController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// "Create a customer account": a patient who does not yet have an account
// creates one themselves. Protected paths NON (we don’t have an account yet, per
// definition):
//
//    POST /registration/acc  ess "Create a customer account" button on the
//                              authentication page: verifies the CAPTCHA from
//                              CETTE page, then opens the form
//    GE T /registrat        ion the form
//    POST /registrati        on the registration process, then returns to the login page
//
// The process is protected against bots by the UN CAPTCHA on the
// authentication page:
//    1. The "Create a Customer Account" button sends the login form
//       to /registration/access; if the CAPTCHA is entered correctly, the server
//       issues a token (see Auth/PasseInscriptionService.cs);
//    2. Without a valid pass, /registration redirects to the
//       authentication page—entering URL directly does nothing;
//    3. The pass is used up upon creation: a solved CAPTCHA
//       allows you to create UN an account;
//    4. In addition, the number of accounts created per hour per IP address is
//       limited (see Auth/LimiteurTentativesService.cs).
//
// The account created is exactly the one that ADMIN would create from the
// "Clients" page (same business-layer method: AjouterClientAsync), if this
// is simply the patient CHOISIT entering their login and password (required,
// with confirmation).
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Metier;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

[Route("inscription")]
public class InscriptionController(
    ApplicationModel application,
    CaptchaService captchaService,
    LimiteurTentativesService limiteur,
    PasseInscriptionService passes) : Controller
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /registration/a  ccess fields: captchaId, captcha (those on the
     // authentication page; username and password, which are also sent, are ignored)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("acces")]
    public IActionResult Acces([FromForm] string? captchaId, [FromForm] string? captcha)
    {
        var ip = AuthController.AdresseIp(HttpContext);

         // too many accounts created recently from this address: no need to proceed further
        var minutes = limiteur.MinutesBlocageInscription(ip);
        if (minutes > 0)
        {
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", new() { ["minutes"] = minutes.ToString() });
            return Redirect("/login");
        }

         // captcha missing or incorrect: return to the authentication page, with
         // a new image (one failure counts as a failed login attempt)
        if (!captchaService.Verifier(captchaId, captcha))
        {
            limiteur.EchecLogin(ip, "");
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT");
            return Redirect("/login");
        }

         // Correct CAPTCHA: Grant access and open the form
        Response.Cookies.Append(PasseInscriptionService.Cookie, passes.Emettre(), PasseInscriptionService.OptionsCookie());
        return Redirect("/inscription");
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /registration
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("")]
    public IActionResult Formulaire()
    {
        if (!ALaissezPasser())
        {
            return RetourLogin();
        }
        return Afficher(new ValeursPersonne());
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /registration
     // The parameter [formulaire] is filled in, and VALIDÉ is replaced by MVC before the call:
     // The validation result is in ModelState.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Creer(FormulaireInscription formulaire)
    {
        if (!ALaissezPasser())
        {
            return RetourLogin();
        }
        var ip = AuthController.AdresseIp(HttpContext);
        var valeurs = new ValeursPersonne
        {
            Titre = formulaire.Titre ?? "Mr",
            Prenom = formulaire.Prenom ?? "",
            Nom = formulaire.Nom ?? "",
            Login = formulaire.Login ?? "",
        };

         // 1. Too many accounts created recently from this address?
        var minutes = limiteur.MinutesBlocageInscription(ip);
        if (minutes > 0)
        {
            return Afficher(valeurs, null, "ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", null, new Dictionary<string, string> { ["minutes"] = minutes.ToString() });
        }

         // 2. All data entry errors at once (fields + confirmation):
             // The user corrects them all at once
        var erreurs = Validation.ErreursDe(ModelState);
        if (!erreurs.ContainsKey("password") && !erreurs.ContainsKey("confirmation") && formulaire.Password != formulaire.Confirmation)
        {
            erreurs["confirmation"] = "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER";
        }
        if (erreurs.Count > 0)
        {
            return Afficher(valeurs, erreurs);
        }

         // 3. Creation (customer + account USER, in a transaction)
        try
        {
             // "!": this tells the compiler that these values are not null -
             // this is true, since the validation ([Required]) was successful
            await application.AjouterClientAsync(new DonneesPersonne
            {
                Titre = formulaire.Titre!,
                Nom = formulaire.Nom!,
                Prenom = formulaire.Prenom!,
                Login = formulaire.Login,
                Password = formulaire.Password,
            });
        }
        catch (MetierException e)
        {
             // username or first name + last name already taken: the pass remains valid
            return Afficher(valeurs, null, e.Cle, Validation.ChampsErreursMetier.GetValueOrDefault(e.Cle));
        }

         // 4. The password has been used: it will not allow you to create a second account
        passes.Consommer(Request.Cookies[PasseInscriptionService.Cookie]);
        Response.Cookies.Delete(PasseInscriptionService.Cookie, new CookieOptions { Path = "/inscription" });
        limiteur.InscriptionReussie(ip);

         // 5. Return to the login page; username is pre-filled
        Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, "INSCRIPTION.DONE", new() { ["login"] = formulaire.Login! });
        return Redirect($"/login?login={Uri.EscapeDataString(formulaire.Login!)}");
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- private methods

    private bool ALaissezPasser() => passes.EstValide(Request.Cookies[PasseInscriptionService.Cookie]);

     // No valid passcode: return to the authentication page
    private RedirectResult RetourLogin()
    {
        Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT");
        return Redirect("/login");
    }

     // The form; the password is never sent back to the browser
    private ViewResult Afficher(
        ValeursPersonne valeurs,
        Dictionary<string, string>? erreurs = null,
        string? erreur = null,
        IEnumerable<string>? autresChamps = null,
        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? erreurParams = null) =>
        View("Inscription", Validation.Preparer(
            new InscriptionModele { TitrePage = "INSCRIPTION.TITLE", Valeurs = valeurs },
            erreurs, erreur, autresChamps, erreurParams));
}

    Let’s comment on this code:

    • lines 14–24: protection against bots, in four steps. The CAPTCHA and attempt limiter were introduced in Example 27;
    • lines 40–45: The controller does not have the [[Authorize]] attribute; its pages are open to everyone. It receives four services via injection;
    • lines 51–52: The “Create a Customer Account” button on the login page sends the login form to this address (attribute [formaction]; see Example 20). Only the CAPTCHA fields are read;
    • line 54: the browser’s address IP, via a static method from [AuthController];
    • lines 57–61: Too many accounts have been created from this address within the last hour: the user is redirected to the login page, with a pop-up message indicating the number of minutes to wait. [new() { ["minutes"] = ... }] creates the message parameter dictionary: its type is inferred from the parameter of [Flash.Deposer];
    • lines 66–70: a missing or incorrect CAPTCHA counts as a failed login attempt (with an empty username): a bot cannot keep trying indefinitely. Returning to the login page displays a new image;
    • lines 74–75: the CAPTCHA is correct: a pass (see [Auth/PasseInscriptionService.cs]) is stored in a cookie, and the browser is redirected to the form;
    • Lines 81–88: the form, only with a valid pass. Typing the address [/inscription] directly is pointless;
    • lines 96–97: creation. The form [FormulaireInscription] (file [Models]) was linked and validated by MVC;
    • lines 99–101: The pass is verified again: the request POST might have been sent without going through the form;
    • lines 104–109: the values to be redisplayed in case of an error, without the password. The default title is [Mr];
    • lines 113–116: the time limit, checked again at the time of creation;
    • lines 121–128: input errors, field by field (see Example 19). The match between the password and its confirmation—which spans two fields—is verified here manually; it is tested only if these two fields are otherwise correct. All errors are reported together: the user corrects them all at once;
    • lines 136–148: creation of the customer and their account USER, using the business layer method employed by ADMIN. If a username or first-name-last-name combination is already taken, the form is re-displayed with the relevant fields highlighted in red; the token remains valid;
    • Lines 152–154: The pass has been used: it is consumed on the server side, and its cookie is deleted. To delete a cookie, you must specify the same path ([Path]) as when it was created: the pass cookie is sent only to addresses [/inscription...]. The creation is finally counted toward the hourly limit;
    • lines 157–158: return to the login page, with the username pre-filled, and a success message. [Uri.EscapeDataString] encodes the username so it can be included in a URL;
    • line 163: the token is read from the request cookie;
    • lines 166–169: if no pass is present, return to the login page with a message;
    • lines 173–181: the form, prepared by [Validation.Preparer], is the same as those for doctors and clients. [erreurParams] is used for the parameters of the footer message (the number of minutes).
